n: Once the people of Ammon settle in Jershon with a church and Nephite armies guarding the borders, Lamanite armies follow them into the wilderness.
The result is the greatest battle the Nephites had known since Lehi left Jerusalem. Tens of thousands of Lamanites are killed and scattered.

f.g: The Nephites keep their promise to protect the people of Ammon, at great cost.

n: Nephite losses are also terrible, but the Lamanites are driven off and the Nephites return home.

f.g: Victory came at a heavy price.

n: Great mourning fills the whole land.
Widows mourn husbands, fathers mourn sons, sisters mourn brothers, sons mourn fathers — grief in every family.
It was a solemn, sorrowful time of fasting and prayer.
So ends the fifteenth year of the judges (about 77 BC).
Mormon closes the account of Ammon and his brothers — their journeys, sufferings, and “incomprehensible joy” — and blesses their souls forever.
He also marks the end of this record of wars, both Nephite civil wars and wars with the Lamanites.
From the first year to the fifteenth, many thousands died — an awful scene of bloodshed.
Many bodies lie buried or rotting in heaps, and many survivors mourn loved ones they fear have gone to endless sorrow.
But others, though grieving, rejoice — they know by the Lord’s promises that their righteous dead are at God’s right hand in never-ending happiness. Faith changes the meaning of grief.

f.w: they rejoice and exult in the hope
at the right hand of God

n: Mormon’s first lesson: sin and the devil’s cunning plans create deep inequality among people — even in how they face death.

f.g: Here, the difference between those who die with hope and those who die without it.

n: His second lesson: there is great need for diligent labor in the Lord’s vineyard. Life holds both sorrow — because of death — and joy, because of the light of Christ.

f.w: labor in the vineyards of the Lord
